---
title: "7.2 Data and sample"
order: 2
---

## Sources

Two files written by the platform's data generator ([D2](../d2-data.qmd)), both for the
booked book only:

| File | Grain | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `shared/data/raw/portfolio.parquet` | one row per booked account: {{< var ews.n_book >}} rows | the account's origination file (the applicant's columns), its on-book state (credit limit, current balance, on-book utilisation, tenure) and the two downstream labels |
| `shared/data/raw/panel.parquet` | one row per account per month, `PANEL_MONTHS` months each (`shared/config.py`) | the monthly behaviour: balance, utilisation, days past due, deposit inflow, overdraft count |

The panel is what makes this model different from the origination models. Everything they
see is a snapshot at application; Early Warning sees how the account has behaved since.

## Features {#ews-features}

`compute_ews_features` (`ews/src/feature_engineering.py`) builds the
{{< var ews.n_features >}} columns of `EWS_FEATURE_COLUMNS`. The first group, `PANEL_FEATURES`,
aggregates the panel account by account, in `_agg_one`:

```python
last3, first6, last6 = df.tail(3), df.head(6), df.tail(6)   # ews/src/feature_engineering.py
first6_dep = max(float(first6["deposit_inflow"].mean()), 1.0)
"util_recent": float(last3["utilization"].mean()),
"balance_recent": float(last3["balance"].mean()),
"deposit_recent": float(last3["deposit_inflow"].mean()),
"util_drift": float(last6["utilization"].mean() - first6["utilization"].mean()),
"deposit_decline_pct": float((first6_dep - last6["deposit_inflow"].mean()) / first6_dep),
"balance_trend": float(last6["balance"].mean() - first6["balance"].mean()),
"util_volatility": float(df["utilization"].std(ddof=0)),
"dpd_months": int((df["days_past_due"] > 0).sum()),
"dpd_max": float(df["days_past_due"].max()),
"dpd_recent": float(last3["days_past_due"].max()),
"overdraft_total": float(df["overdraft_count"].sum()),
"overdraft_recent": float(last6["overdraft_count"].sum()),
```

Levels over the most recent quarter, trends from the first half-year of history to the
last, volatility over the whole history, and counts and worst values of delinquency and
overdrafts. The rest are joined from the portfolio and the scorecard:

| Kind | Columns |
|---|---|
| Behavioural, from the panel | `PANEL_FEATURES`, above |
| On-book state | `utilization_onbook`, `current_balance`, `credit_limit`, `tenure_months` |
| Origination file | `dscr`, `leverage`, `current_ratio`, `prior_delinquencies` |
| The scorecard's output (D4) | `business_score`, `pd_score` |
| Categorical | `industry`, `entity_type` |

The panel aggregation is slow, so `train.py` writes its result to
`ews/models/panel_features.parquet`, committed with the model; the portal, the facts and
`verify.py` read that cache rather than re-aggregating. Every non-categorical column is
made numeric and any missing value becomes zero. The generated data have none, so on this
data the rule changes nothing; on a real book an account with no history would fire no
trigger, and what the model would make of it is untested
([7.7](limitations.qmd#ews-observations)).

`industry` and `entity_type` have no role in how the generator draws deterioration; they are
structural zeros for this target, as `industry` and `entity_type` are for default in D4
(D4 finding 3). Neither is among the model's top {{< var ews.importance.top_n >}} features by
gain ([7.3](methodology.qmd#ews-importance)).

## The label {#ews-label}

The target is `{{< var ews.target >}}`, a 0/1 flag on every booked account. Over the book,
{{< var ews.n_events >}} accounts deteriorate: a base rate of {{< var ews.base_rate >}}.
The generator draws it from a logit of the account's true PD, its recent utilisation above a
level, the rise in its utilisation and its leverage, plus noise, and then a Bernoulli draw:

```python
det_logit = (                                           # shared/data_generator.py
    -2.4
    + 3.0 * pd_true
    + 2.0 * np.clip(util_last3 - 0.85, 0, None)
    + 1.5 * np.clip(util_trend, 0, None)
    + 0.4 * _z(book["leverage"].to_numpy())
    + rng.normal(0, 0.4, m)
)
deterioration = rng.binomial(1, 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-det_logit))).astype(int)
```

Three things follow, each used later in the chapter:

- **Noise enters twice** — the logit's normal term and the Bernoulli draw — so no model can
  rank perfectly. How far the best possible ranking gets is measured in
  [7.5](performance.qmd#ews-ceiling).
- **The strongest driver is not observable.** `pd_true` is the generator's true PD, on the
  leakage deny-list; the bank sees only the scorecard's estimate of it, `pd_score`.
- **The label is drawn from the same simulated history the features summarise.** The name
  says *next*, but in the generator there is no later period: the label
  and the panel are drawn together ([7.4](assumptions.qmd#ews-the-label-looks-forward)).

## Split and seed {#ews-split}

`train.py` draws its own split of the booked book, with the platform seed and stratified on
the label:

```python
X_tr, X_te, y_tr, y_te = train_test_split(               # ews/src/train.py
    X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=SEED, stratify=y)
```

That gives {{< var ews.n_train >}} training accounts and {{< var ews.n_test >}} held-out
accounts (the held-out {{< var ews.test_share >}}), with {{< var ews.n_events_holdout >}}
deteriorations among the held-out: a held-out base rate of
{{< var ews.base_rate_holdout >}}. It is not the scorecard's split — the scorecard splits
applicants, this splits booked accounts. `train.py` records only the model, not which rows
were held out. The facts behind this chapter therefore redraw the split with an indexed call,
check it against an independent call with exactly `train.py`'s arguments, and check its
sizes against the ones `train.py` wrote into `ews/docs/validation_report.md`
(`wiki/facts/ews_facts.py`):

```python
X_tr, X_te, _, _ = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=SEED, stratify=y)
assert (np.array_equal(X_tr.index.to_numpy(), tr)
        and np.array_equal(X_te.index.to_numpy(), te)), \
    "the EWS split no longer reproduces train.py's train_test_split(X, y, ...)"
...
assert (len(tr), len(te)) == report_sizes(), "EWS split no longer reproduces train.py's sizes"
```

`verify.py` redraws the same split the same way to recompute the gate
([7.9](gate.qmd)).

## Leakage controls

The platform's deny-list (`shared/config.py::LEAKAGE_COLUMNS`,
[D2](../d2-data.qmd#leakage-controls)) holds, among others, the target itself, `booked`, and
the generator's true PD. It is enforced for Early Warning at two points:

1. **At feature construction.** `compute_ews_features` raises before returning if any column
   of `EWS_FEATURE_COLUMNS` is on the deny-list:

   ```python
   leaked = [c for c in EWS_FEATURE_COLUMNS if c in LEAKAGE_COLUMNS]
   if leaked:
       raise ValueError(f"Leakage columns in EWS features: {leaked}")
   ```

2. **At training.** `train.py` asserts the same before fitting:

   ```python
   assert set(EWS_FEATURE_COLUMNS).isdisjoint(set(LEAKAGE_COLUMNS)), "leakage in features"
   ```

Unlike the scorecard and adjudication, Early Warning has no test of its own in
`tests/test_leakage.py`; the two checks above run every time the features are built, which
includes every `verify.py` run, so the gap is in the test suite, not in the control
([7.7](limitations.qmd#ews-observations)).

## The score as an input {#ews-score-input}

`business_score` and `pd_score` are not data. `compute_ews_features` calls the scorecard's own
scoring function on the booked accounts:

```python
sp = predict_score_pd(out)                      # ews/src/feature_engineering.py
out["business_score"] = sp["business_score"].to_numpy()
out["pd_score"] = sp["pd"].to_numpy()
```

That is the dependency drawn in [D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd): a change to the scorecard
changes two of this model's inputs and forces a retrain and a recalibration of the tiers
([D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd#what-a-scorecard-change-forces)). It never reads the
generator's true PD. Two properties of the score carry over:

- **It is in-sample for most booked accounts.** The scorecard was fitted on applicants
  outside its held-out {{< var score.test_share >}}, drawn without regard to booking, so a
  booked account's `pd_score` is in-sample for the scorecard unless the account fell in that
  held-out share. The scorecard was fitted on `default`, not on deterioration, and it is a
  binned additive model with little room to memorise; any optimism this lends the held-out
  figures here has not been measured ([7.4](assumptions.qmd#ews-the-score-is-a-valid-input)).
- **D4's findings arrive with it.** How much the model leans on the score, and whether it
  ranks better than the score alone, is measured in [7.5](performance.qmd#ews-benchmark).

## Exclusions

None. Every booked account is in the training or the held-out split, and every booked account
is scored, tiered and flagged by the portal.
